title.narrative: From agents of violence to agents of change - Promoting international humanitarian law with former combatants and police in Myanmar/Myanmar

description.narrative: The proposed 18-month exceptional assistance measure aims to strengthen the role of former combatants and police in promoting respect for non-violence towards civilians in Myanmar. Former combatants and police from the SAC security forces will be guided through a process aimed at shifting their roles from agents of violence during the conflict to advocates for change. The measure will employ a three-pronged strategy, targeting combatants and police at three critical stages: while they are still active in the conflict (conflict parties are increasingly targeted with information on humanitarian norms and the importance of non-violence against civilians); during the defection or surrender process of former combatants and police (reforms of EAOs and NUG policies and procedures on defection and detention to ensure the humane treatment of former combatants, police, and their families); and as they transition into advocates for non-violence towards civilians (former combatants and police increasingly advocate for humanitarian norms, accountability, and non-violence towards civilians). The measure will leverage the insights of former combatants and police to develop context-specific engagement strategies aimed at pro-SAC militia groups. Ultimately, this measure seeks to empower former combatants and police to become key actors in protecting civilians in Myanmar.
